prize_parts.citation: for the design of ionizable lipids and the lipid-nanoparticle formulation methods that enable systemic delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: After the full first round I have changed my preferred configuration: I now propose B058 alone, credited to Cullis, Hope and Madden, and I drop the two-part pairing with B044. B058 was the most widely shared alternative (Aili, Chabes, Linke, Aqvist, Somfai) and no one disputes its science. Its core is a physical-chemical design principle: a lipid whose headgroup pKa keeps it neutral in the circulation, charges it in the acidic endosome, and drives the shift from bilayer to non-lamellar phases that releases nucleic acid into the cytosol. The Vancouver work established that principle, the stable encapsulation of nucleic acids in small particles, and the formulation methods that made systemic delivery reproducible, and the chronology is clear. The chair asked for a defensible three-name allocation, and I think this is one: Cullis, Hope and Madden are the founding trio of both the encapsulation and the ionizable-lipid design, whereas the later lipidoid libraries (Anderson, Langer) and the clinical translation (MacLachlan) extended an established principle. Naming Cullis alone, as I did in round 1, was clean on paper but unfair to Hope and Madden, and several colleagues were right to say so. A single coherent achievement also answers the coherence question better than my round-1 compromise of two parts.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is not fully gone. Anderson and Langer's ionizable lipidoids and MacLachlan's SPLP and DLinDMA work were decisive for the first approved siRNA and mRNA products, and a citation limited to the Vancouver trio will look to part of the community like a priority cut that favours the earlier work over the work that reached patients. Patents and industrial interests overlap in this field, so the committee should anchor the citation in the published lipid-design principle and not in the products. The 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification may be read as having already honoured the delivery side of mRNA vaccines, and Aili and Linke are right that the citation must be about lipid design and delivery, not about mRNA. Lastly, B058 is closer to pharmaceutical science than to pure chemistry for some members, and my own research on lipid self-assembly is near enough that I should not overstate its case.

responses.point: Heiner asked whether the founding formulation work of Hope and Madden outweighs the later combinatorial libraries of Anderson and Langer, said that B058 is the candidate most likely to command a majority if attribution can be settled, and proposed B003 (Miyasaka, Snaith, Park) as his first choice.
responses.response: My answer is yes, for a chemistry prize. The ionizable lipid, the pKa-tuned charge switching and the ethanol-dilution and mixing formulations that give small, stable particles come from the Vancouver group, and the later libraries refined that principle through screening. That is why I now propose Cullis, Hope and Madden and have dropped my own Cullis-only proposal. I agree the citation must be about lipid design and delivery and not mRNA. On B003, I still see the science as real but I cannot get a clean three-name cut among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis, and stability is unproven. B058 now has a better-defined trio than B003. I remain a second-alternative supporter of perovskites.

responses.point: Aili accepts that B058 is chemistry rather than pharmacology and that the pKa-tuned lipid is a molecular design principle, but keeps it as an alternative because three names cannot reconcile Hope and Madden with Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, and because of the 2023 Medicine prize. He is open to moving it up if the committee can agree an allocation.
responses.response: I am taking up that offer by proposing the allocation. My argument is that the three-name limit follows the origin of the principle: encapsulation and ionizable-lipid design came from the Vancouver group, and the lipidoid and translation work extended it. On the 2023 prize, nucleoside modification solved the immunogenicity of the cargo, whereas lipid design solves delivery across the membrane, and both are needed. The two awards cover different chemistry, provided the citation is worded as I do. I accept this is a judgement about credit. I would ask him to say whether he can accept Anderson and Langer being left out if the citation is limited to ionizable-lipid design and formulation.

responses.point: Brzezinski presses on the maturity of B044, since the physiological relevance of some condensates is debated, and says the allocation among six credited names for B058 cannot be resolved within three names and is a serious weakness.
responses.response: On B044 I concede his point: the distinction between equilibrium phase separation in living cells and other assemblies is not yet settled by evidence a prize citation could rely on, and Rosen, Pappu and Mittag's quantitative work would be needed to cover the concept. That, with the fact that no one else supports it, is why I no longer propose it, and keep it only as an alternative. On B058 I reply that the six-name problem is real as a field problem, but the committee does not need to settle it all, only to identify where the principle originated. I think the Vancouver trio does that.

responses.point: Somfai asks of border-field candidates what was new chemically, finds B044 less sharply identifiable than a general catalyst, takes the B058 case more seriously because pKa-tuned ionizable lipids are a molecular design principle, and doubts only the attribution.
responses.response: His chemical-novelty test is fair and B058 passes it, because the novelty is a molecular design rule: the lipid is neutral at physiological pH and ionizes in the endosome. My round-1 point about B021 stands, since I accept that C-N coupling is a distinct advance and a clean two-name case. It remains a second cross-coupling prize within sixteen years, and I still weigh the case for fields with fewer recent awards. I now think B058 passes his chemistry test and has a defined attribution, so I place it above B021.

responses.point: Chabes keeps B028 first on the basis of concrete nucleotide chemistry, now with Balasubramanian and Klenerman only, and has B058 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I welcome his dropping Rothberg, which makes the B028 attribution cleaner than I thought in round 1. My remaining concern is the one Aili and Zou also raised: Ju's terminator chemistry and Mayer's colony sequencing are parallel contributions to the same advance, and a two-name citation will exclude them. I can accept that cut if the committee judges the chemistry, but it is a judgement about the platform and not just the reagents. Since we both support B058 as the nearest alternative, I ask him whether he could vote for it if the committee prefers a Cullis, Hope, Madden allocation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the Cullis, Hope and Madden allocation as the origin of the principle, or considers that leaving out Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan is a priority error.
How much weight the 2023 Medicine prize should carry against delivery lipids, and whether a citation can be worded so that it clearly concerns lipid design and not mRNA.
Whether Brangwynne and Hyman's B044 will become a prize-ready case once the in-vivo evidence for condensates settles, and whether Rosen, Pappu and Mittag must then be credited.
Whether B058 is judged chemistry or pharmaceutical science by the majority.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requires recusal. My research on lipid self-assembly, lipid-protein co-assembly and membrane phase behaviour is close in subject to B058 and B044, and I now advocate B058, so I flag that proximity openly. I have no personal, institutional or funding tie to Cullis, Hope, Madden or any other credited person, and my only institutional tie is that I share Lund with Linke and Somfai, which does not involve a credited person.
